routes.label: Take logarithms and solve a square
Turn the exponent into a square

question: The product of all real roots of the equation \(x^{\log_{10}x}=10\) is
solution:
The logarithm in the equation requires \(x>0\). Taking a base-ten logarithm is useful because it brings down the exponent, producing another factor of \(\log_{10}x\):
\[
\log_{10}\!\left(x^{\log_{10}x}\right)
=(\log_{10}x)^2=\log_{10}10=1.
\]
A real number whose square is \(1\) is either \(1\) or \(-1\). Thus
\[
\log_{10}x=1\quad\text{or}\quad\log_{10}x=-1,
\]
so \(x=10\) or \(x=1/10\).

Both candidates satisfy the original equation: \(10^1=10\) and \((1/10)^{-1}=10\). Every root must be one of these candidates, so their product is
\[
10\cdot\frac1{10}=\boxed{1},
\]
choice A.
